title: C1750 — Daytime running lamp (DRL), LF
introduction:
I use this left-front daytime running lamp reference to distinguish the ground connection from the lamp-control connection. Electrical operation needs a return path as well as the right input—rather like a round trip needing a road home. The assignment table identifies those roles without proving that either path is working.

Start with the connector identification and harness heading. Match each cavity label in the drawing to its Cavity row, then read across for the circuit, wire description, function and terminal identification. The Fpn field beneath the drawing and Terminal Part Number in the assignment table are separate references. Keep the lamp’s side identification and the ground-location wording as printed: they describe different things, and this sheet does not trace the route between them.

This guide teaches the connection map, not lamp access, disconnection, probing or replacement. The physical viewing side, gauge convention and meanings of Size and Used are unspecified. Retain the printed entries; testing requires the applicable setup, expected results and diagnostic branches.

edits.why: The cavity labels are stacked vertically within the rounded opening as drawn. I use the broad curved feature on the picture’s left and stepped outline on its right as recognition landmarks. These are page directions, not instructions for orienting a probe or releasing the physical connector.

Matching each illustrated cavity to its row separates the ground role from the lamp-control role. The ground-location wording does not change the lamp’s stated side. Neither assignment establishes continuity, an expected voltage or the form of the control signal, so the map alone cannot identify the cause of an unlit lamp.
